approaches.clean-worker: fresh worker process: load then eval, killed afterwards
approaches.clean-worker-warm: incremental raco make, then fresh worker load + eval
approaches.one-shot: two plain racket -e processes; Racket loads/compiles on demand
approaches.one-shot-warm: incremental raco make of the target module, then one racket -e

cache-policy: target compiled/ is warm from the compilation block and reused across trials; trials are interleaved with a per-iteration rotation recorded in trial.order
cleanup-definition: workers are tracked and killed in a dynamic-wind, so cleanup runs even if an assertion fails; Worker evaluation timing includes spawn, load, eval AND cleanup, matching one-shot where process exit is inside the measured call
process-definition: direct Racket processes started by the workflow; the measured post-edit path always starts one process, and the excluded pre-edit baseline evaluation starts another; process-tree ownership is not verified
quantile-definition: linear interpolation at rank q*(n-1), rounded to 0.001 ms (CL0-compatible)
scope: real component-logic edits (public export behaviour changes), not injected probes; expected values are declared in the task fixture and checked on baseline and post-edit evaluations
